chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Partial blindness in one eye
summary: He discovered at 13 or 14 he was partly blind in one eye, which hampered reading and ruled out 3-D movies.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: As I look back, one of the things that handicapped me and curtailed my urge to do more reading and writing was the fact that as a child I think I was a ball in one eye, and I didn't become aware that I was partly blind in one eye until I was about 13 or 14 years old. I was a
very good reader, an avid reader, and not only as far as music was concerned, but I loved to read books. But it sort of hampered me in trying to read, because all...
You mean the one eye would get tired.

Yeah, with one eye, you know. And I was very concerned about, you know, the longevity of my sight. Of course, when I went to Europe in the Thirties, I consulted a physician about this, and he told me it was really too late, because the optical nerve had deteriorated to such a point that they just couldn't, you know, do anything about it. So it was a hard thing, but then I resigned myself to it. When three-dimensional pictures came into vogue, I was on the outside because you have to have two eyes, two good eyes, to put the glasses on... You know, they have special glasses for it. You have to have vision in both eyes in order to get the ultimate vision, you know, to enjoy the imagery on the screen.
Well, it's like you really need two ears to appreciate stereo, don't you.
[LAUGHS] But I compensated for that by using my ear, you know. It comes in (?) for playing piano. And I'd see people like Art Tatum, and you know, I could...
